persona.name: Wanchai
persona.background: Rice-farming family in central Thailand's luk thung heartland. Older brother bought Carabao cassettes at the district market; luk thung request programmes on AM radio; Pumpuang and other stars live on stage at temple fairs (ngan wat); Sunday luk thung shows on TV Channel 7; Songkran and New Year songs at school. Isan mor lam only heard when Isan labourers came for the harvest.

Suraphol Sombatcharoen - Nam Ta Lao Wieng
Suraphol Sombatcharoen - Siphok Pi Haeng Khwam Lang

TH1985A.wouldSay: Ue hue lor jang! That's Pumpuang the year she was everywhere, and then Made in Thailand, my brother played that cassette until it stretched.
missing: Pumpuang Duangjan - Khon Dang Leum Lang Khwai (1985)
Pumpuang Duangjan - Ja Hai Ror Por Sor Nai (1982)
TH1985A.fake: The opening is right, but the middle turns into Isan mor lam pieces and 1960s collector rarities (Yenjit Porntawi, Petch Phin Thong) that never played on our radio in 1985.

TH1985B.wouldSay: Made in Thailand, yes, that's us. But then three lam pieces in a row? That's the old Isan ladies' music at a ngan wat, not what we were playing.
missing: Pumpuang Duangjan - Ue Hue Lor Jang (1985)
Pumpuang Duangjan - Khon Dang Leum Lang Khwai (1985)

TH1985B.fake: One Carabao song is followed by a run of traditional mor lam and 1960s compilation rarities, Pumpuang shows up only once, and the 1968 Janis Joplin track was never a Thai hit in 1985.

TH1985C.wouldSay: This is a folk-music record, lam played with khaen. Thai, yes, but where's Carabao, where's Pumpuang? This isn't 1985.
missing: Pumpuang Duangjan - Ue Hue Lor Jang (1985)

persona.name: Oksana
persona.background: Russian-speaking home, Ukrainian at school; father a steelworker at Zaporizhstal. Music came from the M1 and OTV music channels, Hit FM and Russkoe Radio Ukraina in the marshrutka, school discos, and pirated MP3 CDs from the market; Eurovision on TV with the whole family; Orange Revolution songs on the news in late 2004.

seeds.song: Itzhak Perlman & The Klezmatics - Dybbuk Shers
Itzhak Perlman & Klezmer Conservatory Band - Der Heyser Bulgar
Tarras Instrumental Trio - Der glater bulgar

UA2005A.wouldSay: Ruslana, the year after she won Eurovision, then Serduchka and VIA Gra. Yes, that's every school disco I went to.
UA2005A.fake: Only three of twelve seeds are Ukrainian, and a block of four American klezmer recordings from the 1920s to 1990s sits in the middle; that is diaspora heritage music, not anything a Ukrainian teenager heard in 2005.

persona.name: Yelitza
persona.background: Father a por puesto driver, mother a seamstress. Radio Capital and Radio Rumbos on the kitchen radio; Sabado Sensacional on Venevision and RCTV telenovelas; salsa and merengue at block parties and quinceaneras; gaitas and aguinaldos at Christmas; joropo on the radio on national holidays.

seeds.song: José Luis Rodríguez - Dueño de Nada
Juan Vicente Torrealba - Concierto en la Llanura
Diomedes Díaz - Cariñito de Mi Vida

VE1985A.wouldSay: Louis! Franco De Vita on the radio every hour, then El Puma, then Caballo Viejo. That's my mother's kitchen in Catia.
missing: Guillermo Dávila - Sólo pienso en ti (early 1980s)
VE1985A.fake: The strong local opening gives way to three Colombian tracks and only four Venezuelan seeds out of nine, with no Oscar D'León salsa or gaita; and the vallenato is credited to Diomedes Díaz, who wrote it, when the hit recording was Rafael Orozco's with Binomio de Oro.
suspect: Diomedes Díaz - Cariñito de Mi Vida
